title: Staggered rollout heuristics and crosswalk notes (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
A lightweight working reference for coordinating staggered rollouts and small-batch canaries across product, SRE, infra, and solutions teams. This is intentionally pragmatic — short heuristics, crosswalks of responsibilities, and low-friction ops scripts we can iterate from during launches.

Context / motivation:
- We are shipping more LLM-driven features that require heterogenous inference (hosted + dedicated + private). Different slices have different latency/cost tolerance and regulatory needs.
- Current postmortems repeatedly surface gaps: unclear ownership when latency climbs during canaries, mismatched signal definitions across teams, and noisy A/B slicing that causes oscillation.
- Goal: reduce human coordination overhead, shorten time-to-safe-activation, and standardize what counts as a safe signal.

High-level principles (short):
1) Safety ladder: smoke -> micro-slice -> traffic ramp -> global. Each rung has explicit signals and minimum stability windows.
2) Signal parity: define 3 cross-team signals (latency P95, error-rate, semantic-regression) with agreed instrumentation before exposure.
3) Fast rollback first: automated soft-fallback to a compatible model variant or lower-cost tier as the first response.
4) Small, meaningful slices: prefer persona or device-based slices that map to business risk rather than purely random samplings.
5) Cost-aware gating: if unit-token cost > threshold AND latency degraded, throttle exposure even if quality is nominal.

Operational crosswalk (who does what):
- Product (feature PM): hypothesis, target slice definitions, acceptance criteria for quality and business metrics, comms owner.
- Platform/Infra: capacity prechecks, autoscale knobs, quantization/variant readiness, synthetic traffic harness.
- SRE/Observability: telemetry dashboards, fast alerts, rollback automation hooks, post-launch retrospective owner.
- Solutions/CS: customer-facing rollback comms, prioritized customer list to exclude/include in canary.
- DevX/Console: rollout config, A/B toggles, cohort routing rules, experiment metadata.

Minimum checklist before lift (pre-launch):
- schema-locked: rollout config saved in repo + change-reviewed (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- load rehearsal: run 15m synthetic at expected p50/p95 QPS on canary infra and confirm kube/GPU headroom.
- telemetry: latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, error categories, safety signals (toxicity flag rate), and semantic-regression score available on console.
- experiment plan: slice sizes, sampling method, seed for randomization, statistical power note if using A/B.
- rollback path: documented model variant fallback, traffic switch commands, and oncall contact list.

Signal definitions (shared canonical):
- Latency: p95 measured at the API boundary (includes queueing). Gate if p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.6 for 10m rolling window.
- Error rate: 5xxs + model-timeouts. Gate if > baseline_rate + 0.75% absolute for 5m.
- Semantic regression (quality): run small gold-set evals on sampled responses (BLEU/ROUGE not enough). Gate if average quality drop > 6% over baseline for 30m.
- Safety regressions: any spike in safety labels (content-moderation triggers) > 2x baseline for 15m must auto-throttle and notify policy lead.

Staged activation recipe (example):
1) Smoke (internal): 0.1% traffic, internal users only, 10m observation. Primary checks: p95 and 5xxs.
2) Micro-slice: 0.5% named cohort (beta customers), 30m observation. Add quality eval and cost telemetry.
3) Ramp phase 1: 5% randomized, 1h observation; ensure autoscale events within budget and no oscillation.
4) Ramp phase 2: 25% regional, 2h observation with real-time dashboarding.
5) Full activation: 100% with gradual TTL for config (e.g., 6h anneal where we keep guardrails active).

A/B testing notes (pragmatic):
- If A/B is powered for product metrics (e.g., conversion), record required N and window; otherwise treat as quality experiment and use paired-quality tests.
- Prefer deterministic routing keys (user_id hash) to reduce contamination across multi-device sessions.
- Use blocking flags for training data leakage experiments — do not let canary responses leak into model retraining pipelines without explicit filters.

Automation primitives we need (short list):
- traffic-shift CLI: single command to shift X% from variant A->B with optional dry-run.
- short-lived synthetic workloads generator per-service to reproduce latency spikes.
- auto-throttle rule builder: UI to compose simple threshold rules (latency/cost/error) and preview impact.

Quick operator playbook (when alarm fires):
1) Read the alert: check the exact signal and scope.
2) Run quick isolation: shift 90% of slice traffic off the canary variant (traffic-shift CLI).
3) If traffic shift fails or latency persists, fall back to safe-model variant (documented).
4) Triage: pair product + infra + SRE for 30m triage; log artifact IDs and start a decision log.
5) Post-incident: short rectification meeting within 48h and update this doc with findings.

Example rollback command snippets (ops notes):
- CLI: rwctl rollout shift --from featureX-v2 --to featureX-v1 --percent 90 --dry-run=false
- Console quick action: "revert cohort" button (must be guarded behind 2FA + oncall ack).

Measuring experiment health (suggested dashboard):
- Top: exposure % by cohort and model variant.
- Left: latency p50/p95 trend for each variant.
- Middle: error rate and token-unit-cost per request.
- Bottom: quality eval over gold set (rolling), safety label rate, and customer-impact flags.

Edge cases & unresolved tradeoffs:
- Multi-tenant oscillation: how aggressive should global throttles be versus per-tenant quarantines? (open question; preference: per-tenant isolation first).
- Statistical contamination from transient retries: retries inflate effective exposure. Need to account for deduped user-exposure when sizing experiments.
- Private deployments: customers on Private may not surface telemetry to central console; define a handshake protocol for manual gating.

Open items / next actions:
- (Priya) draft a lightweight JSON schema for rollout metadata (owner, slices, signals, fallback commands).
- (Ethan) prototype rwctl traffic-shift command and share PR by 2025-02-10.
- (Ada) add a gold-set authoring checklist in observability and wire up auto-eval.
- (Saira) run one cross-team tabletop sim next week and capture failure modes.

Notes for retrospective capture (post-activation template):
- time window of instability, impacted cohorts, root cause hypothesis, immediate remediation steps taken, time to recovery, follow-up action owners.

Quick comms templates (short):
- To customers (if impacted): "We detected increased latency for feature X between hh:mm and hh:mm. Traffic was automatically shifted to a stable variant. We are investigating and will follow up by EOD."
- Internal alert thread starter: "CanaryAlert: feature X | p95 up 2.1x | cohort=beta-users | immediate action: traffic shifted -> rollback in progress. Oncall: @sre-oncall"

Appendix: micro-simulation experiment (how to sanity-check exposure):
- run 3 back-to-back 30m sims: baseline load, +30% QPS, burst 10x for 60s at minute 20. Observe orchestration latency and GPU queue growth.

This doc is intentionally compact — prefer iterating small concrete tools and checklists rather than another long canonical playbook. Add items, experiment results, and concrete CLI/UI links below.

---
Decision log snippets (latest):
- 2025-01-22: agreed to adopt p95*1.6 latency gate across product and infra for canaries (owner: SRE).
- 2025-01-28: agreed rollout metadata schema draft (owner: Priya).

End of notes.

(Unresolved: finalize exact thresholds for private deployments and how to handle multi-region partial outages.)
